Twenty-four comments

This tune is adorable isn’t it? It’s more or less the version played at a recent Sydney session by site member bandjalong - (ta for the tune). It is related to an Amix tune called “The Drunken Tinker” which has a similar 1st part. Confusingly, that tune sometimes also goes by the name of “The Yellow Tinker”, e.g. on Altan’s album “The Red Crow”.

I’m willing to bet that “The Drunken Tinker” came about because a drunken session player tried to remember “The Yellow Tinker”, and could only remember the 1st part of the 3, so he/she made up a new 2nd part. Or maybe not.

↳ Posted by Dr. Dow on March 30th, 2003.

Sheetmusic readers watch out for the key changes

↳ Posted by Dr. Dow on March 30th, 2003.

Modal reels

Loads of fun. Melodic contours in the 1st part are nearly the same for both “Tinkers.” The Drunken Tinker in Amix falls more comfortably on my mandolin. Lots of open A string to ring through.

The Gmix is more interesting though. Now I must learn both tunes so I can get them mixed up. :-)

↳ Posted by Gra5ity on March 31st, 2003.

The Amix one is at https://thesession.org/tunes/1555

The Yellow Tinker, X:7

As played by Eamon Cotter, Conor McCarthy, Oisin MacDiarmada & Padraic O’Reilly
on track 11 of “The Riches of Clare”. I think this is an old Clare setting of the Yellow Tinker that probably
pre-dates Paddy O’Brien’s famous version. I think Noel Hill taught us this version at one of his concertina schools, too. I like it a lot. It can be played all on the C-row of the concertina.
(There is no B in the tune, so it doesn’t matter whether there is a B-flat in the key signature or not.)

↳ Posted by ithaca-markb on June 24th, 2019.

The Yellow Tinker, X:8

Basic transcription (transposed in Gmix) from Cormac Begley’s playing in his album “Cormac Begley” (https://thesession.org/recordings/5633). Track available here:

https://cormacbegley.bandcamp.com/track/reels-yellow-tinker-ri-l-mho-r-bhaile-an-chalaidh

Cormac plays the tune in Dmix, I have transposed it in Gmix which seems to be the original key and fits well on the flute.

A video recording of Cormac playing the tune is available here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R0rjZJ4OdsA

(Edit: I see this movie was already posted above. Great playing, anyway!)

↳ Posted by Sergio Rampino on December 22nd, 2020.

The Yellow Tinker, X:17

Paddy O’Brien from Tipperary recorded this tune in the early 1950s and this setting is based on that recording. I am not aware of an earlier recording of this reel and his setting is reckoned to have inspired many a musician. There are some noticeable differences in this version, that I have based on Paddy’s recording, from others posted here. Needless to say I found his recording uplifting, and it reminds me of listening to one Bro. Aiden from Ipswich playing it one morning at the Fleadh in Buncrana and loving the snap in the third part.

↳ Posted by brailsford on November 10th, 2025.
